examples.en: Our police station has jurisdiction over this area.
Which department is in charge of this matter?

examples.ko: 시청이 관할하는 공원이라서 청소를 자주 해요.
examples.en: It's a park under city hall's management, so it gets cleaned often.
The court will have jurisdiction over that issue.
The area the fire station used to cover changed last year.

examples.ko: 시청에서는 자기들이 관할하지 않는 일은 도와줄 수 없다고 했어요.
examples.en: City hall said it can't help with things outside its jurisdiction.

explain: '맡다'는 일상에서 아무 일에나 쓰지만 관할하다는 경찰서·구청 같은 기관이 권한을 가진 구역이나 업무에만 써요. 보통 '~이/가 관할하다'로 쓰고, 뉴스와 공문서에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: '맡다' (take charge) works for any task, but 관할하다 is only for an agency such as a police station or district office that holds authority over an area or duty. It usually appears as '~이/가 관할하다' in news and official documents.

examples.en: I insert a picture in the middle of the document.
I added a video to the presentation.
Which button do I press to insert a table?

examples.ko: 문장 사이에 쉼표를 삽입한 사람이 누구예요?
examples.en: Who put the comma between the sentences?
I'll insert the photo later.

examples.ko: 파일 이름 뒤에 날짜를 삽입하고 저장했어요.
examples.en: I added the date after the file name and saved it.

explain: 컴퓨터 문서에서 그림이나 표를 넣을 때 '삽입'이라는 메뉴를 자주 봐요. 물건을 안에 넣을 때는 일상에서 '넣다'를 쓰고, 삽입하다는 문서·기계·글처럼 격식 있는 상황에 어울려요.
explain_en: You often see a menu called '삽입' when adding pictures or tables in a computer document. For everyday objects Koreans say '넣다' (put in); 삽입하다 fits documents, machines, and writing in a more formal setting.

examples.en: The president promoted Manager Kim to department head.
The company promotes employees with good results.
My team leader wrote a recommendation to get me promoted.

examples.ko: 그 사람을 승진시킬 거라는 소문이 있어요.
examples.en: There's a rumor they'll promote that person.

examples.ko: 열심히 일한 직원을 승진시키는 회사가 좋아요.
examples.en: I like companies that promote hard-working employees.

examples.ko: 왜 그분만 승진시키고 다른 사람은 안 올려 줘요?
examples.en: Why do they promote only that person and not the others?

explain: '승진하다'는 내가 올라가는 것, 승진시키다는 회사나 윗사람이 올려 주는 것이에요. 그래서 '제가 승진했어요'와 '사장님이 저를 승진시켰어요'처럼 주어가 달라지고, 올라가는 사람에는 '을/를'을 붙여요.
explain_en: 승진하다 is when you move up yourself; 승진시키다 is when the company or a superior moves someone up. So the subject changes: '제가 승진했어요' (I got promoted) vs '사장님이 저를 승진시켰어요' (the boss promoted me), and the promoted person takes '을/를'.

examples.ko: 공기 중에는 아주 작은 입자가 떠다녀요.
examples.en: Tiny particles float around in the air.

examples.ko: 이 가루는 입자가 고와서 물에 잘 녹아요.
examples.en: This powder has fine particles, so it dissolves well in water.

examples.ko: 과학 시간에 물질을 이루는 입자를 배웠어요.
examples.en: In science class we learned about the particles that make up matter.

examples.ko: 이 필터는 큰 입자만 걸러 줘요.
examples.en: This filter only catches large particles.
They say light sometimes moves like a particle too.

examples.ko: 눈에 안 보이는 입자들이 하늘에 가득해요.
examples.en: The sky is full of particles you can't see.

explain: '미세먼지 입자', '입자가 곱다·굵다'처럼 입자는 과학이나 뉴스에서 아주 작은 알갱이를 말할 때 써요. 일상에서 가루나 모래 알갱이는 보통 '알갱이'라고 해요.
explain_en: 입자 shows up in science and news, as in '미세먼지 입자' (fine-dust particle) or '입자가 곱다/굵다' (fine/coarse grain). In daily talk, grains of powder or sand are usually just '알갱이'.

examples.en: The airline delays departure because of the rain.

examples.ko: 회사는 월급 지급을 한 달 지연했어요.
examples.en: The company delayed paying salaries by a month.
If you keep putting off work, it gets hard later.

examples.ko: 공사를 지연할 수밖에 없는 이유가 있어요.
examples.en: There's a reason we have no choice but to delay the construction.
I want to fix my habit of delaying replies.

examples.ko: 서류를 늦게 내서 심사를 지연하고 말았어요.
examples.en: I submitted the documents late and ended up delaying the review.

explain: '늦어지다'는 저절로 늦어지는 것이고, 지연하다는 누군가가 늦추는 느낌이에요. 안내 방송에서는 '열차가 지연되고 있습니다'처럼 '지연되다'를 더 많이 들어요.
explain_en: '늦어지다' is something running late by itself, while 지연하다 feels like someone is causing the delay. In announcements you more often hear the passive '지연되다', as in '열차가 지연되고 있습니다' (the train is delayed).

examples.en: The shop writes its opening hours out front.
How did you write this word in English?
You have to print the expiration date on the product.

examples.ko: 외국 이름을 한글로 표기할 때 헷갈려요.
examples.en: I get confused when writing foreign names in Hangul.
Please come to the spot marked on the map.
They list the allergy ingredients on the menu.

explain: '쓰다'보다 격식 있고, 글자·기호·숫자로 어떻게 나타내는지를 말할 때 써요. '한글로 표기하다', '영어로 표기하다'처럼 방식을 같이 말하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It is more formal than '쓰다' (write) and is used for how something is shown in letters, symbols, or numbers. It often comes with the method, as in '한글로 표기하다' (write in Hangul) or '영어로 표기하다' (write in English).

examples.en: The stairs continue in a spiral shape.
The spiral on this shell is pretty.
The smoke rose, drawing a spiral.

examples.ko: 나선처럼 도는 길을 따라 산에 올랐어요.
examples.en: I climbed the mountain along a path that winds like a spiral.
It's a spiral staircase, so it's hard to climb.

examples.ko: 나선은 자연에서 자주 볼 수 있는 모양이에요.
examples.en: Spirals are a shape you often see in nature.

explain: '나선형 계단', '나선 은하'처럼 나선은 다른 말 앞에 붙어서 많이 써요. 원은 처음과 끝이 만나지만 나선은 끝이 열려 있어요. 일상에서는 '빙글빙글', '소용돌이'라고 하기도 해요.
explain_en: 나선 is often attached before another word, as in '나선형 계단' (spiral staircase) or '나선 은하' (spiral galaxy). A circle closes on itself, but a spiral stays open at the end. In daily talk people also say '빙글빙글' (round and round) or '소용돌이' (whirl).

examples.en: Only fragments of that memory remain.
I found a fragment of the story in an old letter.

examples.ko: 주말에 단편 영화를 한 편 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched a short film on the weekend.
It's hard to judge from only fragmentary information.
My favorite writer's short stories are excellent.

examples.ko: 이 책에는 짧은 단편들이 모여 있어요.
examples.en: This book is a collection of short pieces.

explain: 단편은 '단편 소설'처럼 짧은 이야기일 수도 있고, '기억의 단편'처럼 전체 중 일부 조각일 수도 있어요. '단편적으로 알다'는 조금만 안다는 느낌이라 좋은 평가는 아니에요. 긴 이야기는 '장편'이라고 해요.
explain_en: 단편 can be a short work as in '단편 소설' (short story), or a piece of a whole as in '기억의 단편' (a fragment of memory). '단편적으로 알다' means knowing only bits, which is not a compliment. The long counterpart is '장편'.

examples.en: I show all my ability on test day.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 결승에서 놀라운 힘을 발휘했어요.
examples.en: That player showed amazing strength in the final.

examples.ko: 위기가 오면 용기를 발휘할 수 있을까요?
examples.en: Will I be able to show courage when a crisis comes?
Please give me a chance to show what I can do.

examples.ko: 이 약은 먹으면 곧 효과를 발휘하기 시작해요.
examples.en: This medicine starts to take effect soon after you take it.
I was nervous and couldn't show my usual skill.

explain: 실력·능력·용기·효과처럼 안에 있던 좋은 것을 밖으로 보일 때 써요. '실력을 발휘하다', '능력을 발휘하다'처럼 같이 쓰는 말이 거의 정해져 있고, 나쁜 것에는 잘 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It is for good things that were inside you coming out, such as skill, ability, courage, or an effect. It pairs with fixed words like '실력을 발휘하다' and '능력을 발휘하다', and it is rarely used for bad things.

examples.ko: 그 군인은 나라의 수호를 위해 일해요.
examples.en: That soldier works to defend the country.

examples.ko: 환경 수호에 관심 있는 학생들이 모였어요.
examples.en: Students interested in protecting the environment gathered.
Protecting cultural heritage is everyone's job.
Protecting human rights is this group's goal.
Nothing is as important as safeguarding peace.

examples.ko: 그들은 전통의 수호와 발전을 함께 이야기했어요.
examples.en: They talked about both protecting and developing tradition.

explain: 나라·평화·인권·문화처럼 큰 가치를 지킨다는 무거운 느낌이라 뉴스나 연설에서 자주 나와요. 일상에서 물건이나 자리를 지킬 때는 '지키다'를 써요. 동사로는 '수호하다'를 많이 써요.
explain_en: 수호 carries a weighty feel of defending something big such as a country, peace, human rights, or culture, so it appears in news and speeches. For everyday things like objects or a seat, use '지키다'. The verb form is 수호하다.

examples.en: Firefighters protect citizens' safety.
We have to protect our cultural heritage.
He defended his beliefs to the end.
I'm grateful to the soldiers who defend the country.

examples.ko: 환경을 수호할 방법을 같이 생각해 봐요.
examples.en: Let's think together about ways to protect the environment.

examples.ko: 약한 사람의 권리를 수호하고 싶어서 변호사가 됐어요.
examples.en: I became a lawyer because I wanted to defend the rights of the weak.

explain: '지키다'와 같은 방향이지만 수호하다는 나라·평화·권리처럼 크고 소중한 것에 써요. 약속을 지키다, 자리를 지키다처럼 일상의 것은 '지키다'를 써야 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It points the same way as '지키다' (keep/guard), but 수호하다 is for big, precious things such as a nation, peace, or rights. For everyday matters like keeping a promise or holding a seat, '지키다' sounds natural.

examples.en: This company transports fruit across the country.
A truck carried the goods to the port.
Frozen food has to be transported cold.

examples.ko: 큰 기계를 운송할 배를 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for a ship to carry the large machine.
It takes two days to ship the cargo.

examples.ko: 비행기로 꽃을 운송하고 나서 바로 팔았어요.
examples.en: After flying the flowers in, they sold them right away.

explain: '나르다'는 손이나 작은 차로 옮기는 느낌이고, 운송하다는 트럭·배·비행기로 많은 짐을 멀리 보내는 일에 써요. 택배·물류 회사 이야기에서 자주 들려요.
explain_en: '나르다' feels like moving things by hand or in a small vehicle, while 운송하다 is for sending a lot of cargo far by truck, ship, or plane. You hear it often when talking about parcel and logistics companies.

examples.en: We draw lots to pick who gets the prize.
We drew the winners yesterday.
I'll tell you right away once they draw the numbers.

examples.ko: 추첨하는 모습을 인터넷으로 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can watch the drawing online.
We drew lots for seats and then sat down.
We'll hold the drawing for the event gifts tomorrow.

explain: '뽑다'는 아무거나 고르는 일에도 쓰지만 추첨하다는 운에 맡겨 당첨자나 순서를 정할 때 써요. 뽑힌 사람은 '당첨되다'를 써요. 이벤트·기숙사·청약처럼 결과가 운으로 정해지는 곳에서 자주 들려요.
explain_en: '뽑다' (pick) can mean choosing anything, but 추첨하다 is for leaving it to luck to decide winners or order. The person who is chosen is '당첨되다'. You hear it for events, dorm rooms, and housing lotteries where luck decides.

examples.en: A reporter covers the accident scene.
Our newspaper covered that incident.
I went at dawn to interview the people at the market.
I only write articles from what I've reported myself.
I'm going to cover the players tomorrow.
I heard many stories while reporting.

explain: 기자나 방송 작가가 기사를 쓰려고 현장에 가서 사람을 만나고 자료를 모을 때만 써요. 일반인이 정보를 찾을 때는 '조사하다'나 '알아보다'를 쓰고, 취재하다를 쓰면 기자가 된 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is used only when a journalist or broadcast writer goes to a scene, meets people, and gathers material for a story. Ordinary people looking things up say '조사하다' or '알아보다'; using 취재하다 makes you sound like a reporter.

examples.ko: 두 회사가 합작해서 새 자동차를 만들었어요.
examples.en: Two companies teamed up and built a new car.
Korean and Japanese directors co-produce the film.

examples.ko: 친구들과 합작하면 더 좋은 작품이 나올 거예요.
examples.en: If you collaborate with friends, a better work will come out.
The drama co-produced by two countries is popular.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 다른 학교와 합작할 계획이에요.
examples.en: Our team plans to collaborate with another school.

examples.ko: 서로 도우며 합작하는 일이 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: Collaborations in which people help each other are increasing.

explain: '같이하다'는 누구와도 쓰지만 합작하다는 회사·나라·예술가가 힘을 합쳐 영화·제품·사업 같은 결과물을 만들 때 써요. '~와/과 합작하다'로 말하고, '합작 영화', '합작 회사'처럼 명사 앞에도 많이 붙어요.
explain_en: '같이하다' (do together) works with anyone, but 합작하다 is for companies, countries, or artists joining forces to make a film, product, or business. It is used as '~와/과 합작하다' and often sits before nouns, as in '합작 영화' and '합작 회사'.

examples.en: This is regarded as a serious mistake.

examples.ko: 늦게 오면 결석으로 간주될 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you come late, it can be counted as an absence.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 최고의 가수로 간주되고 있어요.
examples.en: That person is considered the best singer.

examples.ko: 연락이 없으면 포기한 것으로 간주되니까 꼭 답해 주세요.
examples.en: No reply counts as giving up, so please be sure to answer.
That method was regarded as the safest.

examples.ko: 신고하지 않으면 동의한 것으로 간주되는 규칙이에요.
examples.en: It's a rule that not reporting counts as agreeing.

explain: '생각하다'와 달리 간주되다는 실제와 상관없이 규칙이나 사회가 그렇다고 보는 경우에 써요. '결석으로 간주되다'처럼 규칙·계약 문장에서 자주 보여요. 말할 때는 '~로 봐요', '~로 쳐요'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: Unlike '생각하다' (think), 간주되다 is used when a rule or society treats something as so, whatever the facts are. It appears in rules and contracts, as in '결석으로 간주되다' (counted as absent). In speech people more often say '~로 봐요' or '~로 쳐요'.

examples.en: My family resides in Seoul.
This area is comfortable for people to live in.

examples.ko: 오래전부터 이 마을에 주거한 사람들을 만났어요.
examples.en: I met people who have lived in this village for a long time.
More people live in high-rise buildings now.
I have no plan to live in the mountains.
He lived abroad and came back last year.

explain: '살다'가 일상 대화의 말이고, 주거하다는 서류·뉴스·부동산 글에서 격식 있게 쓸 때 어울려요. 비슷한 '거주하다'가 더 흔하고, 주거는 '주거 공간', '주거 환경'처럼 명사로 더 자주 써요.
explain_en: '살다' is the everyday word; 주거하다 suits documents, news, and real-estate writing in a formal tone. The similar '거주하다' is more common, and 주거 is used more often as a noun, as in '주거 공간' (living space) and '주거 환경' (living environment).

examples.en: A free lecture is held at the district office hall.
Let's meet in front of the village hall.
The student hall has a cafeteria and a snack shop.
That hall is old, so it's being repaired.
I took the bus to the citizens' hall.
The neighbors cleaned the hall together.

explain: 모임·행사·강연을 위해 지은 건물 이름에 붙어요. '시민회관', '학생회관', '마을회관'처럼 앞에 누가 쓰는지 붙이고, 영어의 '홀'이나 '센터'와 비슷하지만 한국에서는 공공 건물이라는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It attaches to the names of buildings made for meetings, events, and lectures, with the users in front, as in '시민회관', '학생회관', and '마을회관'. It is close to English 'hall' or 'center', but in Korea it has a public-building feel.

examples.en: The school posts the test results on the notice board.
I posted the notice on the website.
Get permission before you post a photo.
We need a place to put up the notice.
I want to delete the post I made.
I put the closing day on the shop door and left work.

explain: 누구나 볼 수 있게 게시판이나 웹사이트에 올려 두는 일에 써요. 온라인에서는 '올리다'가 일상적이고, 게시하다는 공지·규정 같은 공식 글에 더 어울려요. 올라온 글은 '게시글', '게시물'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is for putting something on a notice board or website where anyone can see it. Online, '올리다' (upload) is the everyday word, and 게시하다 fits official posts such as notices and rules. A posted item is called '게시글' or '게시물'.

examples.ko: 이 마을 근처에 오래된 광산이 있어요.
examples.en: There is an old mine near this village.

examples.ko: 광산에서 일하는 사람들은 힘든 일을 해요.
examples.en: People who work in mines do hard work.
After the mine closed, people left.
That mine was famous for coal.
I was shocked to see the news about the mine accident.
The road to the mine is blocked.

explain: '탄광'은 석탄을 캐는 광산이고, 금광·은광처럼 캐는 것에 따라 이름이 달라져요. 지금은 문을 닫은 광산을 박물관이나 관광지로 쓰는 곳도 많아요.
explain_en: A '탄광' is a coal mine, and the name changes with what is dug, such as '금광' (gold mine) and '은광' (silver mine). Many closed mines are now used as museums or tourist spots.

examples.en: The bridge suddenly collapsed.
There is a risk that the old building will collapse.
When it rains a lot, the mountain road gives way.

examples.ko: 시장이 붕괴하는 바람에 많은 회사가 문을 닫았어요.
examples.en: Because the market collapsed, many companies closed.

examples.ko: 붕괴한 곳에서 구조 작업이 계속되고 있어요.
examples.en: Rescue work continues at the site of the collapse.

examples.ko: 믿음이 붕괴하고 나서 둘은 다시 만나지 않았어요.
examples.en: After their trust collapsed, the two never met again.

explain: '무너지다'는 건물·마음·벽 어디에나 쓰는 일상어이고, 붕괴하다는 뉴스에서 건물·제도·경제처럼 큰 것이 무너질 때 써요. 명사 '붕괴'는 '붕괴 사고'처럼 자주 보여요.
explain_en: '무너지다' (fall down) is the everyday word for buildings, hearts, or walls; 붕괴하다 is used in the news for big things collapsing, such as a building, a system, or an economy. The noun 붕괴 often appears as in '붕괴 사고' (collapse accident).

en: begin; get started in; take up

examples.en: I took up yoga last year.
I signed up at an academy to get into guitar.
More people are taking up golf.

examples.ko: 클라이밍에 입문한 지 두 달 됐어요.
examples.en: It's been two months since I started climbing.
I'm just about to start learning to cook.

examples.ko: 그림에 입문해서 매일 한 장씩 그려요.
examples.en: I got into drawing and draw one every day.

explain: 취미·운동·학문 앞에 '~에 입문하다'로 써요. '시작하다'보다 이제 막 그 세계에 들어선 느낌이 있어요. 책 제목의 '입문'은 처음 배우는 사람을 위한 책이라는 표시예요.
explain_en: It is used as '~에 입문하다' after a hobby, sport, or field. Compared with '시작하다' (start), it gives the feeling of having just stepped into that world. '입문' in a book title marks it as a book for beginners.

examples.en: Lawmaking is an important job of the National Assembly.

examples.ko: 새 법을 만드는 입법 과정을 배웠어요.
examples.en: I learned about the legislative process of making new laws.
Citizens are demanding new legislation.
Legislation takes longer than I thought.
The legislation was delayed, so the problem grew.

examples.ko: 입법과 행정은 서로 다른 일을 해요.
examples.en: Legislation and administration do different jobs.

explain: 입법은 법을 집행하는 '행정', 법으로 판단하는 '사법'과 짝으로 배워요. '입법 활동', '입법 과정', '입법부'처럼 뒤에 붙는 말과 함께 뉴스에 많이 나와요.
explain_en: 입법 is learned as a set with '행정' (administration, carrying out laws) and '사법' (the judiciary, judging by law). It appears in the news with words like '입법 활동', '입법 과정', and '입법부' (the legislature).

examples.ko: 이 색과 저 색이 잘 조화돼요.
examples.en: This color and that color go well together.
The building that blends tradition and modernity looks great.
When the two flavors blend well, it tastes better.
The clothes and bag didn't match, so I changed them.
I saw an ad where the music and video work together.

examples.ko: 팀원들의 의견이 조화될 때까지 회의를 했어요.
examples.en: We kept meeting until the team members' opinions came together.

explain: '어울리다'는 사람·옷·음식에 두루 쓰는 말이고, 조화되다는 둘 이상이 부딪치지 않고 하나로 균형을 이룰 때 써요. '~와/과 조화되다', '조화된 ~'로 쓰고, 어울리다보다 글에서 더 자주 보여요.
explain_en: '어울리다' (suit/go with) is used broadly for people, clothes, and food; 조화되다 is for two or more things balancing into one without clashing. It is used as '~와/과 조화되다' or '조화된 ~', and shows up more in writing than 어울리다.

examples.en: In the old days, people made roofs out of straw.
The farmer piled up the straw.
Once straw gets wet, it doesn't dry easily.
Grandmother wrapped the eggs in straw and gave them to me.
It's a country village that smells of straw.
Even straw rots when it gets old.

explain: 짚은 벼 같은 곡식을 거두고 남은 마른 줄기라서 지붕·신발·새끼줄 같은 시골 물건에 쓰였어요. '짚신', '짚단'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙을 때가 많고, '지푸라기'는 짚의 작은 조각을 말해요.
explain_en: 짚 is the dry stalk left after harvesting rice or other grain, so it was used for country items such as roofs, shoes, and rope. It often attaches before another word, as in '짚신' (straw sandals) and '짚단' (straw bundle), and '지푸라기' is a small piece of straw.
